gaps.title: Dynamic intended use / behavioral envelope
gaps.explanation: GenAI systems may move between informational, recommendatory, and action-directing behavior over the course of a conversation.

gaps.title: Human-AI system performance
gaps.explanation: The clinically relevant unit of performance may often be the combined human-AI system rather than the model alone.

gaps.title: Deployment assurance & scalability
gaps.explanation: The same product may perform differently across populations, workflows, EHR configurations, local data, users, and safeguards. FDA needs a clearer framework for what manufacturers establish globally and what deploying organizations must validate locally.

gaps.title: Operational harm
gaps.explanation: Over-escalation, rework, unnecessary utilization, clinician burden, and workflow disruption may matter even where classic device harm is absent.

gaps.title: Evidence burden & commercial viability
gaps.explanation: Continuous benchmarking and clinical validation can improve assurance, but regulatory obligations may become economically unscalable if they are not proportional to risk and product value.

gaps.title: AI supplier quality
gaps.explanation: Foundation model companies function increasingly like critical suppliers whose changes can alter regulated product behavior.

gaps.title: Cybersecurity as clinical safety
gaps.explanation: Prompt injection, tool manipulation, retrieval poisoning, and related vulnerabilities can become direct clinical hazards.

gaps.title: Distributed accountability
gaps.explanation: Manufacturers, foundation-model developers, platform vendors, health systems, and clinicians may each control different parts of the safety system.

gaps.title: Delegated authority
gaps.explanation: Agentic systems raise a distinct question: what actions has the organization actually delegated to the AI, and how far can an error propagate before meaningful human intervention?
